name: Kent Peterson
bio_short: Kent Peterson is a Newburgh-based painter and printmaker whose abstracted works draw on geology and anthropology. He is a longtime participant in Holland Tunnel Gallery exhibitions and programs its Cinema Club.
bio_long: Kent Peterson is a painter and printmaker who lives and works in Newburgh, New York. According to Holland Tunnel Gallery, his abstracted paintings and prints draw on geology and anthropology, and his work is held in private and public collections in the New York area. He has been part of the gallery's circle since its Williamsburg years: he was one of 110 artists in Framed (2014), the Stairmasters project that marked the gallery's 17th year in Brooklyn. He showed in the Grand Opening of Holland Tunnel Newburgh in May 2018 and in that year's holiday art sale. In 2019 he took part in the 9th Annual Newburgh Open Studios. In fall 2020 he showed with Marieken Cochius and Romina Gonzales in Terra / Derma, and in summer 2023 he appeared with Gerda van Leeuwen and Peter Yamaoka in Down To Earth, which the gallery described as a show by a trio of masters of color, texture and abstraction. His painting Untitled (1986) was featured in the announcement. Peterson is also the film programmer for the gallery's Cinema Club, choosing the classic films screened at 46 Chambers Street.
practice: Abstracted paintings and prints inspired by geology and anthropology, with close attention to surface, texture and process (per Holland Tunnel Gallery).

verification.evidence: Holland Tunnel sources are consistent: he is a Newburgh painter and printmaker, is in the artist list, and appears in Framed 2014, the 2018 opening, Terra/Derma, Down To Earth and the Cinema Club. NewburghNY.org lists him in the 2019 Newburgh Open Studios. I found no independent bio, website or birth details, and the name is shared with others (e.g. a California muralist), so the bio stays within what the gallery says.
